question: Does a frozen foundation backbone with a linear head, trained only on real photos and their autoencoder reconstructions, detect images from a generator family it never saw (Kandinsky 2.2) better than the fine-tuned DINOv2 and DINOv3 models?
scope_limit: Real photograph versus AI-generated image only. Nothing here says whether a watch is genuine.

training_data.real: Label_0 train split of split_manifest_v2.json, the first 1,000 per brand in manifest order (5,000 photos)
training_data.fake: Each of those photos passed through two public autoencoders: stabilityai SD 1.5 VAE (runwayml/stable-diffusion-v1-5/vae, fp16) and SDXL VAE (stabilityai/stable-diffusion-xl-base-1.0/vae, fp32). Encode, take the latent mode, decode. No text prompt and no diffusion sampling.

image_pipeline.base: EXIF transpose, RGB, centre-crop to square, Lanczos resize to 512 x 512. Reconstruction happens on this base image.
image_pipeline.augmented_view: with p = 0.5 resize by a factor U(0.5, 1.0) and back (bicubic); with p = 0.3 Gaussian blur radius U(0.2, 1.5); JPEG quality uniform integer 60-95. Seeded per sample and view; identical rules for real and fake.
image_pipeline.train_views: clean and augmented, for real and both reconstructions
image_pipeline.evaluation_views: clean only. Benchmark images (already 768 x 768 JPEG q90) go through the same base + clean step.

candidates.clip_vitl14_linear: openai/clip-vit-large-patch14, frozen, L2-normalised projected image embedding (768-d), logistic regression
candidates.dinov3_vitb16_linear: timm vit_base_patch16_dinov3.lvd1689m pretrained weights (not the HypeVault fine-tune), frozen, 512 input, pooled CLS (768-d), logistic regression

classifier: scikit-learn LogisticRegression, standardised features, C = 1.0, class_weight balanced, max_iter 5000. Not tuned.
selection: Validation only. Label_0 validation split (200 per brand, clean) against Label_1 validation split (200 per brand, clean). Label_1 is a generator neither candidate trained on. Higher ROC-AUC is selected.
threshold: 99th percentile of P(fake) on the 1,000 Label_0 validation photos, so about 1% of our real validation photos are rejected. Fixed before the final evaluation.

final_evaluation.primary: benchmark_v1 REAL_PHOTO (300 eBay photos) + heldout_kandinsky22 (284). Kandinsky's decoder was never used.
final_evaluation.secondary: benchmark_v1 sdxl_base10 (150). The SDXL decoder was used in training, so this set is NOT unseen for the new model.
final_evaluation.in_distribution: Label_0 test (1,506) and Label_1 test (1,500) of split_manifest_v2.json
final_evaluation.metrics: detection rate of generated images and false-fake rate on real photos at the fixed threshold, with exact Clopper-Pearson 95% intervals; ROC-AUC
final_evaluation.comparison: benchmark_v1 run 20261020T110244Z results for dinov2_legacy and dinov3_experimental on the same images

success_criterion: Kandinsky detection at the fixed threshold is higher than the best earlier model (DINOv3: 12/284 FAKE) with non-overlapping 95% intervals, while the false-fake rate on the 300 eBay real photos stays at or below 5%.
